strengths: Clear identification and empirical demonstration of the Jensen's Gap problem in PDE-constrained diffusion models, with effective synthetic experiments (MoG, Stokes) illustrating the phenomenon
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8+ PDE benchmarks with multiple metrics, thorough ablations, compute-matched comparisons, and diverse downstream tasks (forward, inverse, reconstruction)
Efficient one-step generation achieving 100-5000x speedup over baselines while maintaining or improving physical constraint satisfaction
Method naturally supports multiple downstream tasks within a single framework, which prior methods do not provide
Thorough appendix with additional ablations on component attribution, diversity preservation, teacher quality sensitivity, architecture robustness, and dynamic weighting
Honest discussion of limitations and acknowledgment that distributional fidelity claims remain empirical
weaknesses: Theoretical justification is limited: Theorems B.1-B.2 rely on simplified assumptions (low-rank Gaussian, diagonal score networks) with significant gap from actual nonlinear PDE problems; no formal proof that final-sample supervision preserves learned distributions

Distributional fidelity claims lack rigor: FPD metric computed on PDE-learned representations rather than verifying overall sample distribution preservation; diversity metrics (Table 7) don't guarantee samples from same distribution

Improvements are modest and inconsistent: Statistical errors (MMSE/SMSE) often similar or worse than teacher; compute-matched gains over DiffusionPDE are limited; PIDDM-1 requires refinement for strong results

Limited novelty: Applies well-established distillation techniques (Rectified Flow, DMD) to a new domain; enforcing constraints on final samples rather than intermediate estimates is relatively straightforward
Overclaimed minimal hyperparameter tuning: λ_train ranges 10-10⁶ across datasets; Figure 3b-c shows noticeable sensitivity; dynamic weighting required for stiff PDEs despite robustness claims

Jensen's Gap demonstration has limitations: MoG experiment is artificial; Stokes experiment shows increased loss but causality not definitively established; could other factors explain the observation?

Incomplete failure mode analysis: Limited exploration of behavior with noisy/approximate PDE operators, when teacher retraining is needed, or scalability to high resolutions (all experiments at 128×128)

Missing implementation details: Computational cost of teacher sampling not detailed; total training time not reported; code availability not mentioned; masking strategy interaction with physics constraints not theoretically analyzed

strengths: Clear empirical demonstration of Jensen's Gap problem with synthetic datasets (MoG, Stokes) providing concrete motivation
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8+ PDE benchmarks with consistent metrics and thorough ablation studies (Tables 1-4, Appendix G)
Practical efficiency: one-step generation (1 NFE) vs. 100+ NFE for baselines, valuable for deployment
Consistent PDE error improvements (5-10x reduction across most benchmarks)
Well-written paper with extensive reproducibility details in appendices (32 pages total)
Unified framework supporting forward problems, inverse recovery, and reconstruction through single model
weaknesses: Distributional fidelity claims acknowledged as 'empirical' with no theoretical justification for why final-sample distillation preserves teacher's distribution; Theorems B.1-B.2 analyze specific cases but don't explain this fundamental property

Limited technical novelty: applies existing distillation methods + PDE loss on final samples—straightforward engineering rather than fundamental contribution; Jensen's Gap already recognized in prior work (PIDM, DiffusionPDE)
Critical dependence on teacher quality underexplored; starting with vanilla diffusion (which lacks constraints) as teacher seems suboptimal; if teacher has violations, student inherits them

PIDDM-1 (one-step, no refinement) underperforms on generative quality metrics (e.g., Poisson SMSE: 0.326 vs. ECI 0.291); claimed efficiency gains require 80 refinement steps (PIDDM-ref), reducing practical advantage

Hyperparameter tuning oversold despite claims of 'minimal' tuning: λ_train varies 10→10⁶ across datasets (1000x range), λ_infer per task required, refinement steps and step sizes need tuning; contradicts claimed robustness

Superficial theoretical analysis: Theorem B.1 shows expected intuitive result; Theorem B.2 is straightforward convex optimization; Appendix B.3 uses simplified diagonal Gaussian setting far from real PDE problems; missing convergence guarantees and sample complexity analysis

Incomplete baseline comparisons: D-Flow unfairly penalized with 5000 NFE, teacher baseline is vanilla diffusion (not physics-informed), baselines adapted from authors' codebase, no multi-seed error bars or statistical significance testing

Jensen's Gap 'solution' overstated in title and framing: PIDDM sidesteps rather than solves the gap; if teacher has constraint violations, student inherits them; distributional implications not clearly established

strengths: Well-motivated problem: Jensen's Gap in PDE-constrained diffusion is clearly identified and rigorously demonstrated through analytical MoG experiments, training-time analysis on Stokes, and intuitive explanation (Section B.3)
Simple and practical method: Post-hoc distillation with final-sample PDE enforcement is elegant, straightforward to implement, and combines standard components effectively

Comprehensive experimental validation: 8 diverse PDE benchmarks (elliptic/parabolic/hyperbolic/nonlinear), multiple task types (forward/inverse/reconstruction), consistent order-of-magnitude improvements in PDE residual error

Strong empirical results: PIDDM-1 achieves 1 NFE with competitive statistical metrics; PIDDM-ref outperforms all baselines on constraint satisfaction; compute-matched comparison (Table 3) shows advantages even with equal budget

Thorough ablations and analysis: Component attribution (Table 6), diversity preservation (Table 7), teacher quality sensitivity (Table 8), architecture robustness (Table 9), convergence/stability (Tables 11-12) clarify design choices
Honest limitations discussion: Authors acknowledge distributional fidelity claims remain empirical, require well-trained teacher, and admit hyperparameter tuning still needed
Comprehensive appendix: Theoretical analysis (Theorems B.1-B.2), detailed experimental setup, multiple datasets, baseline implementations support reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited theoretical justification: Theorems B.1-B.2 apply only to simplified low-rank Gaussian setting; gap between toy 2D analysis and 128×128 grid PDEs is substantial; no analysis of failure modes or when method underperforms

Overclaims about hyperparameter robustness: Abstract claims 'minimal hyperparameter tuning' but λ_train varies 100× across datasets (10 vs 10⁶ for Helmholtz/Poisson); Figure 3(b) shows sensitivity; Table 10 requires dynamic weighting—contradicts minimal-tuning narrative

Dependence on teacher quality: Method requires well-trained teacher with diversity; Table 8 shows gains saturate after 6k iterations but convergence depends on dataset; no systematic guidance for when teacher is 'ready'

Limited distributional improvements: FPD scores sometimes worse than teacher (Poisson: 1.281 vs 1.342); paper doesn't claim strong distributional gains (honest but limits scope); one-step distillation inherently loses distributional information

Incremental novelty: Distillation of diffusion models established (Liu et al. 2023); adding PDE loss to student straightforward; core insight (enforce at final sample not posterior mean) is intuitive rather than deep innovation

Incomplete Jensen's Gap analysis: Figure 2c shows DPS fails but doesn't fully explain why PIDDM solves it; Theorem B.2 shows teacher outputs still have violations; Section B.3 explanation via score sharpness is informal and lacks rigor

Hard constraint masking (Eq. 6) ad-hoc: Borrows mask mixture from ECI without theoretical justification; Table 4 shows it matters empirically but why this formulation improves F satisfaction unclear; feels like practical hack

Limited scope: All tested PDEs show improvements—may not capture difficult cases; scalability to resolutions >128×128 unknown; comparisons mostly use FNO (U-Net/CNN only in Table 9 appendix); no comparison with improved non-diffusion baselines
